summary.tldr: Adds presumptions in the Criminal Code for using force, including lethal force, to defend a person in a dwelling-house.
what_it_does: Clarifies that a person may use force, including lethal force, that they deem reasonably necessary to defend or protect themselves or another person against an unlawful entrant in a dwelling-house.
Creates a presumption that a person who knowingly enters a dwelling-house without legal right did so with intent to use force against a lawful occupant, unless there is evidence otherwise.
Presumes the conditions for the defence of person are met when a lawful occupant uses force, including lethal force, against an unlawful entrant in the dwelling-house.
who_it_affects: People lawfully present in a dwelling-house
summary.background: The bill amends section 34 of the Criminal Code, which deals with the defence of person.
